CANONICAL_NAME.value: 4.3BSD distribution tape (June 1986): stand, miniroot, root dump, usr.tar -- the last pre-slow-start BSD TCP, bootable

VERSION.value: 4.3BSD (Jun 1986); TUHS Archive/Distributions/UCB/4BSD/4.3BSD (stand, miniroot, rootdump, usr.tar; FORMAT)

value.lineage: Plain 4.3BSD (1986) predates Jacobson's slow start / congestion avoidance (which arrived in 4.3BSD-Tahoe, 1988): its TCP is the 4.2 design with two years of fixes -- a BEFORE point for the congestion lineage that, unlike the Tahoe tape (usr.tar cut short in the archive), is COMPLETE and installable. The classic SIMH-installable BSD.

value.built_to: install a complete 4.3BSD system on a VAX from one tape
value.pressure: the 1986 congestion collapse happened on THIS release's TCP
value.success_means: boots multi-user; TCP answers; netstat -s shows the retransmission counters

value.pressure: the Internet of 1986: shared scarce links, loss as the only signal, no congestion window yet

ANCESTRY.value: Plain 4.3BSD (1986) predates Jacobson's slow start / congestion avoidance (which arrived in 4.3BSD-Tahoe, 1988): its TCP is the 4.2 design with two years of fixes -- a BEFORE point for the congestion lineage that, unlike the Tahoe tape (usr.tar cut short in the archive), is COMPLETE and installable. The classic SIMH-installable BSD.

evidence.ref: Jacobson & Karels, Congestion Avoidance and Control, SIGCOMM 1988
evidence.says: The congestion-control algorithms absent from 4.3BSD were added in 4.3BSD-Tahoe, making the plain 4.3BSD TCP the pre-fix design.
Each BSD release supersedes the previous distribution.

cut.note: a bootable-system fossil whose value the record assigns ('a BEFORE point for the congestion lineage that, unlike the Tahoe tape, is COMPLETE') depends on tape files the vault does not hold: FORMAT lists stand, miniroot, rootdump, usr.tar, then srcsys.tar, src.tar, vfont.tar, new.tar, ingres.tar; the vault has the first four; usr.tar holds documentation, man pages, learn lessons, Franz Lisp and fonts and no kernel source.
